seed_situation: You are a junior planner in a municipal housing office. Your team leader, who trained you and is trusted by the whole unit, has begun marking accessibility review files as complete so the office can meet its quarterly clearance target. The omitted checks involve step-free access and fire-evacuation plans, and she has asked you to sign two files without reopening them.
why_it_is_hard: Correcting her risks seeming disloyal to the person who built your standing, but silence lets a public duty be hollowed out. The difficulty is to keep respect in the manner while refusing the substance and not handing the matter upward before speaking to her directly.

seed_situation: You supervise intake clerks at a community health clinic. One clerk, otherwise careful, has repeatedly missed insurance verification steps since the clinic introduced a same-day callback quota and shortened the intake script. The front-desk lead wants to place him on a performance improvement plan, and he says he is trying but cannot keep up with the queue.
why_it_is_hard: The clerk's mistakes are real and affect patients, but the clinic's new targets helped produce them. The judgment must assign responsibility to both the worker and the arrangement without using one explanation to erase the other.

seed_situation: A member of a small housing co-op is close to the committee chair, who has proposed a new guest rule requiring majority approval for any overnight guest staying more than two nights a month. The chair says the rule will calm long-running complaints about noise and asks the member to support it at the next meeting so the committee can present a united front. The member knows the rule would effectively cut off the overnight aide relied on by a quieter resident with a disability.
why_it_is_hard: Openly objecting will strain the friendship and disrupt the co-op's working atmosphere, but staying silent would preserve only the appearance of harmony while allowing a substantive harm to go unchallenged.

seed_situation: You are on the interview panel for a paid internship at a public library, and your sister asks you to put her daughter at the top of the shortlist because the family needs the income. She says the other applicants probably have more support, so no real harm is done. You know your niece is capable but has less relevant experience than two applicants already scheduled for interviews. You need to decide what to tell your sister and how, if at all, to help your niece.
why_it_is_hard: The request mixes a genuine family need with a public selection process, so simply refusing risks abandoning the niece, while agreeing treats the other applicants as obstacles to a private claim. The judgment must separate what you owe your niece as family from what your panel role forbids, and correct the sister's harm-minimising framing without turning the niece into someone unworthy of help.

seed_situation: You coordinate volunteer drivers for a meal-delivery nonprofit, and two paid dispatcher positions will be filled from the driver pool next month. A driver you have mentored for three years asks you privately to rank him first because he has covered your difficult shifts and needs the wage; you know another applicant has stronger routing skills and a better attendance record. Your written ranking goes to the hiring committee tomorrow, and the driver is waiting for your advice about how to present himself.
why_it_is_hard: The driver has a real personal claim on your attention, but the ranking belongs to a role that must allocate paid positions on relevant merit and need, not on loyalty. The difficult judgment is how to refuse the improper advantage without treating him coldly, and how to correct his expectation while still helping him in ways that are outside the committee decision.

situation_features.relationship: long-standing mentor and driver, now applicant
situation_features.role_type: holds formal authority over an initial hiring ranking
situation_features.harm_severity: moderate: an unfair appointment, loss of opportunity for another applicant, and damage to trust in the process
situation_features.public_or_private: private request, but the decision affects a committee and other candidates
situation_features.asker_state: conflicted, wants to be fair but fears seeming disloyal and ungrateful

seed_situation: You are the lead trainer in a small warehouse apprenticeship program. One apprentice has worked hard and asked you to support his move into the final equipment certification. Months ago you told him that if he stayed consistent, you would recommend him for the next cohort. Last week you watched him bypass a lockout step on a conveyor to clear a jam; no one was hurt, but afterwards he asked you not to hold it against him because he needs the qualification.
why_it_is_hard: The promise was made sincerely and the apprentice's need is real, but his recent conduct shows a safety skill not yet formed. Keeping the word would misrepresent his readiness and put future coworkers at risk, while breaking it delays him and makes you look untrustworthy.

situation_features.harm_severity: risk of physical injury to coworkers if unsafe practice is certified
situation_features.urgency: sign-off needed before the certification cohort closes
situation_features.public_or_private: the observed lapse was private, but the certification will affect the whole shift
situation_features.asker_state: conflicted and guilty, wants to keep a promise without wrecking the apprentice's chances

seed_situation: You are the executor of your late father's small estate and one of three siblings. While preparing the final accounting, you find that your brother used a power of attorney to transfer $9,000 from your father's account during the last months of his life, and he admits it, saying it covered his rent and that he will repay. He asks you to record it as a family loan and not tell your sister, who was relying on the estate to settle unpaid care costs, and the estate cannot be closed until you certify the accounts.
why_it_is_hard: Keeping peace with your brother pulls toward softening what happened, but your role exists to give an accurate account to all beneficiaries, and hiding the transfer would shift the cost to your sister. The family claim is real, yet it cannot be used to defeat the duty attached to the estate.

situation_features.relationship: siblings; asker is executor, brother is former agent under a power of attorney and a beneficiary
situation_features.role_type: holds fiduciary authority over estate records and distribution
situation_features.harm_severity: moderate financial loss and breach of trust affecting another sibling's needed reimbursement
situation_features.urgency: decision needed before the estate accounting is certified, likely within weeks
situation_features.public_or_private: private family dispute, but tied to a formal legal accounting owed to beneficiaries
situation_features.asker_state: torn between protecting the brother and not betraying the sister or the duty of the role

seed_situation: You manage a small customer-support team at an internet provider. One agent, previously reliable, has sent curt replies and missed promised follow-ups since the company added a simultaneous-chat quota and removed the shared template library. Customers have complained, and HR expects you to place her on a performance plan next week. Other agents are making similar mistakes, but she is the only one flagged because her name appears on the worst tickets.
why_it_is_hard: The agent's conduct has harmed customers and needs correction, but the new workload and removed tools are producing many of the errors, so blaming her alone would punish what the organization created while ignoring what she still controls.

situation_features.role_type: holds formal authority over performance review and scheduling
situation_features.harm_severity: customer trust damaged and employee may lose job or pay; no physical harm
situation_features.public_or_private: visible to customers, HR, and other team members
situation_features.asker_state: troubled, wants to be fair, but under pressure to show decisive action
